synthesizedFacts.fact: Both lupus and rosacea can cause a butterfly-shaped malar rash on the face.
Lupus is an autoimmune disease that can affect multiple organs, while rosacea is primarily a skin condition affecting the face.
A malar rash in lupus may appear as reddish or salmon-colored dots with white outer circles, while rosacea may present with raised blood vessels.
Rosacea is the most common cause of a malar rash, but lupus is a significant differential diagnosis.
